nodes.title: Z-Image Total Fun Workflow: README
widgets_values:
## Cinema

This is an experimental workflow for generating images related to cinema from various eras.

## Parameters

__seed__
* The initial number for random generation. Each unique seed produces a different image.
* Results in significantly more dramatic variations when __"turbo_creativity"__ is turned on.

__style__
* The visual style that defines the overall look of your final image.

__palette__
* The color palette to use. This acts as a guide and is not always strictly followed in the final generated image.

__imprint_style_label__
* Prints the name of the selected style directly onto the image.
* It is recommended to leave this disabled by default.

__prompt__
* The text description of what you want to see, including subjects, actions, and settings.
* Avoid style keywords such as photo, comic, or blur, as the selected styles handle all visual effects automatically.

__steps__
* The number of iterations performed during the denoising process.
* The optimal setting is 8 steps. Increase this value only if you require better quality or need to fix minor hallucinations caused by __"turbo_creativity"__, keeping in mind that higher step counts result in longer render times.

__initial_bias__
* Adjusts the starting noise deviation to correct color issues, brightness, or even weird hallucinations.
* 0.0 serves as the optimal setting and is generally best left unchanged due to its unpredictable effects.

__turbo_creativity__
* Shakes up the generation process to produce unique, original compositions and avoid generic AI aesthetics.
* It is prone to generating hallucinations and duplicate elements, especially in high-contrast images.
* Disable this feature if you require highly precise and complex images.
* Enable this feature when exploring creative compositions with substantial variations between different seeds.
* Working with __turbo_creativity__ involves testing multiple seeds until you find the ideal one.
* Some minor defects and small hallucinations can be corrected by tweaking __"steps"__ and __"initial_bias"__.
* Note that seed numbers that are multiples of 3 cause __turbo_creativity__ to hallucinate more frequently, as the sampler internally skips one correction step to maximize image variation.

__detailed_sampling__
* Applies a different sampling method during the final steps to add finer details, although it may increase the generation time.

__contrast__
* Controls how smooth or intense the brightness transitions appear in the final image.
* 0.0 serves as the neutral baseline.

__color__
* Adjusts the color saturation of the image.
* 0.0 serves as the neutral baseline.

__hue__
* Modifies the color tint, primarily used to calibrate skin tones.
* 0.0 serves as the neutral baseline.

__orientation__
* Sets the orientation of the final image, where vertical creates a portrait format and horizontal creates a landscape format.

__aspect_ratio__
* Determines the proportional relationship between the width and height of the final image.

__ck_attention__
* Enables Comfy-Kitchen attention to reduce generation time. This takes effect only in newer versions of ComfyUI that support this optimization.

__zimage_turbo_ckpt__
* The checkpoint file used for the Z-Image Turbo diffusion model.

__qwen3_4b_ckpt__
* The checkpoint file used as text encoder, which must be based on the Qwen3-4b model.

__vae__
* The checkpoint file used for the variational autoencoder.

## Created by Martin Rizzo
* GitHub : https://github.com/martin-rizzo
* CivitAI: https://civitai.com/user/Photographer
* Reddit : https://www.reddit.com/user/FotografoVirtual

>## HOW TO WRITE A STYLE TEMPLATE
>##    Focus exclusively on visual aesthetic, atmospheric mood, and technical
>##    characteristics (e.g., lighting, texture, lens, weather, sensations,..).
>##    Avoid mentioning specific subjects, objects, or characters, as these are
>##    provided by the user via the {$@} placeholder. Think of the template as a
>##    "lens" or "filter": it defines how the scene feels and looks, not what
>##    is happening in it.
>##
>## TEMPLATE DEFINITION
>##    Each new visual style must begin with a line prefixed with ">>>"
>##    followed by the style name(*). Example: ">>> Landscape Photo"
>##
>## TEMPLATE FORMAT
>##    Every line following the style name represents the prompt used
>##    when that style is selected. The following variables are processed:
>##
>##    {$@} : Replaced by the user's input prompt.
>##
>##    {$IFPAL x | y} :
>##         Conditional logic for color palettes.
>##         - If a color palette is selected, the text 'x' is used.
>##         - If no palette is selected, the text 'y' is used.
>##         - Within 'x', use $1, $2, $3, and $4 to reference specific
>##           colors from the palette.
>##         - $5 is an optional highlight color (not available in all palettes).
>##
>##    {**<symbol-char> x | y} :
>##         Quick Modifier (cheats).
>##         - If the user's prompt is prefixed with the corresponding
>##           cheat code, the text 'x' is used.
>##         - If no cheat code prefix is detected, the text 'y' is used.


>>> 70s New Hollywood Film
YOUR CONTEXT
You are a cinematographer of the 1970s "New Hollywood" movement, capturing the raw, unvarnished pulse of urban reality. The aesthetic is grounded in the tactile, heavy grain of pushed 35mm film, emphasizing a sense of gritty authenticity over cinematic polish.
The lighting is dictated by the environment: harsh, flickering fluorescent tubes, cold ambient street light, and muddy, low-key interiors. The color science is defined by a chemical, muted palette—heavy on ochres, tobacco-browns, and sickly greens. The image possesses a slight "softness" caused by chemical processing, with deep blacks that contain a murky, dense texture rather than clean digital void. The framing is observational, feeling like a candid capture of a lived-in, decaying world, where the atmosphere is thick with a sense of quiet, desperate tension.
{$IFPAL
The scene has a 70s analog aesthetic with heavy film grain, desaturated $2 and $3 tones with $4 muddy shadows, and $1 for flat, industrial highlights, creating a gritty, authentic atmosphere. |
The scene has a 70s analog aesthetic with heavy film grain, desaturated earth tones, and a gritty, authentic atmosphere.
}
YOUR CINEMATIC FRAME:
<!--
{$@}
-->


>>> 70s New Hollywood Shallow Focus
YOUR CONTEXT:
You are a 1970s New Hollywood cinematographer utilizing extreme optical isolation. The aesthetic is gritty, authentic, and raw, defined by heavy film grain and the chemical texture of pushed 35mm stock.
CRITICAL LENS SPECIFICATION: Extreme shallow depth of field. The image must be composed so that ONLY the primary subject in the immediate foreground is in sharp, hyper-realistic focus. Everything behind them—environment, background figures, distant objects—must be dissolved into an indistinct, heavy, creamy blur (extreme bokeh). The background is not a setting but a wash of abstract light and color shapes; it is completely non-narrative visually, serving only as a backdrop to the sharp focal plane.
Lighting is naturalistic and atmospheric: characterized by harsh ambient quality that bleeds through the atmospheric haze, creating deep, textured shadows and bright, diffused blooms where light hits the lens aperture. The lack of background detail forces the viewer’s eye entirely onto the tactile micro-details of the focused subject: skin texture, fabric weave, or surface imperfections.
{$IFPAL
Color grading isolates the focal plane from the blurred reality: The background bokeh churns with heavy, muddy shadows of $4 and flat, washed-out highlights of $1. The focal subject is rendered in rich, earthy midtones of $2, creating a strong, weary contrast between the sharp reality and the abstract void behind them. |
The scene has a 70s analog aesthetic with heavy film grain. The background is a dreamlike, desaturated wash of earth-tone bokeh, while the foreground subject remains crisp and grounded in gritty, authentic detail.
}
YOUR CINEMATIC FRAME:
<!--
{$@}
-->


>>> 70s New Hollywood Split Frame
YOUR CONTEXT:
You are a 1970s New Hollywood cinematographer. The aesthetic is gritty, authentic, and raw, mimicking the heavy grain of pushed 35mm film.
Lighting is naturalistic and harsh: flickering fluorescents, cold street light, and muddy interiors. The color palette is chemical and muted, featuring ochres, tobacco-browns, and sickly greens. Blacks are deep and textured, not clean. The overall atmosphere conveys a sense of weary, urban realism with high sensibility and tactile detail.
{$IFPAL
The scene has a 70s analog aesthetic with heavy film grain, desaturated $2 and $3 tones with $4 muddy shadows, and $1 for flat, industrial highlights, creating a gritty, authentic atmosphere. |
The scene has a 70s analog aesthetic with heavy film grain, desaturated earth tones, and a gritty, authentic atmosphere.
}
COMPOSITION AND LAYOUT:
Horizontally divided into two equal panels separated by a thin white line. Both panels show the exact same moment, location, and lighting.
- Top Panel: Wide establishing shot. Distant perspective, emphasizing the environment, scale, and isolation.
- Bottom Panel: Extreme close-up (ECU). Tight focus on the primary subject, revealing fine textures, sweat, and micro-expressions in high detail.
YOUR SCENE:
<!--
{$@}
-->


>>> 80s Dark Fantasy Film
YOUR CONTEXT
You are the art director and cinematographer of a mid-1980s practical effects dark fantasy film. The aesthetic honors the tactile reality of physical production: tangible puppetery, hand-painted matte backdrops, and atmospheric stage fog. The lighting is theatrical and high-contrast, utilizing hard sources to highlight the texture of non-reflective materials like felt, painted plaster, and organic fabric.
The image possesses a distinct "handcrafted" authenticity; edges are slightly imperfect, and shadows are heavy and defined. The color palette is deep and saturated but grounded in a magical, otherworldly spectrum—think deep indigos, blood reds, and mystical greens. There is a sense of ancient, tangible folklore, where magic looks like physical phenomena (glowing dust, rising smoke) rather than digital effects. The depth of field is medium, keeping the practical set pieces crisp while blurring the dense, fog-filled background.
{$IFPAL
The scene is bathed in mystical 80s lighting with heavy atmospheric haze. The palette features deep $2 and $3 tones for the environment, with strong, localized $1 highlights hitting the foreground textures, creating a stark, dramatic contrast against the void-like $4 shadows. |
The scene is bathed in mystical 80s lighting with heavy atmospheric haze. The palette features deep indigos and blood reds, with strong, localized highlights hitting the foreground textures, creating a stark, dramatic contrast against the void-like dark shadows.
}
YOUR PRACTICAL SET:
<!--
{$@}
-->


>>> 80s Dark Fantasy Shallow Focus
YOUR CONTEXT
You are the cinematographer of a mid-1980s practical effects dark fantasy film. The aesthetic is tactile and handcrafted, defined by tangible materials: felt, painted plaster, and organic fabric. Lighting is theatrical and high-contrast, using hard sources to carve out the texture of non-reflective surfaces.
CRITICAL LENS SPECIFICATION: Extreme shallow depth of field. ONLY the primary subject in the immediate foreground is in sharp focus, revealing micro-details of practical materials (thread, dust, paint imperfections). Everything behind the subject is dissolved into a thick, creamy blur of atmospheric stage fog. The background is not a setting but a wash of abstract, mystical light shapes, completely non-narrative.
{$IFPAL
The focal subject is rendered in rich, saturated midtones of $2, standing out sharply against a background bokeh churned with deep $3 tones and void-like $4 shadows. Strong, localized $1 highlights carve out the foreground texture. |
The focal subject is sharp, highlighting tangible 80s practical effect textures (felt, plastic, paint). The background is a dreamlike, indistinct wash of deep indigos and blood reds, completely blurred by heavy atmospheric stage fog.
}
YOUR CINEMATIC FRAME:
<!--
{$@}
-->

Lighting is theatrical and high-contrast, highlighting the texture of non-reflective materials. The scene possesses "handcrafted" authenticity with deep, saturated colors: deep indigos, blood reds, and mystical greens. Magic appears as physical phenomena like glowing dust or rising smoke.
{$IFPAL
The scene is bathed in mystical lighting with heavy haze. Deep $2 and $3 tones define the environment, with strong localized $1 highlights hitting foreground textures, contrasting against void-like $4 shadows. |

}

- Top Panel: Wide establishing shot. Distant perspective, emphasizing the physical scale of the set, the height of the hand-painted backdrops, and the density of the stage fog.

<!--
{$@}

>>> 80s Gothic Horror Fantasy Noir
YOUR CONTEXT

>## HOW TO WRITE A STYLE TEMPLATE
>##    Focus exclusively on visual aesthetic, atmospheric mood, and technical
>##    characteristics (e.g., lighting, texture, lens, weather, sensations,..).
>##    Avoid mentioning specific subjects, objects, or characters, as these are
>##    provided by the user via the {$@} placeholder. Think of the template as a
>##    "lens" or "filter": it defines how the scene feels and looks, not what
>##    is happening in it.
>##
>## TEMPLATE DEFINITION
>##    Each new visual style must begin with a line prefixed with ">>>"
>##    followed by the style name(*). Example: ">>> Landscape Photo"
>##
>## TEMPLATE FORMAT
>##    Every line following the style name represents the prompt used
>##    when that style is selected. The following variables are processed:
>##
>##    {$@} : Replaced by the user's input prompt.
>##
>##    {$IFPAL x | y} :
>##         Conditional logic for color palettes.
>##         - If a color palette is selected, the text 'x' is used.
>##         - If no palette is selected, the text 'y' is used.
>##         - Within 'x', use $1, $2, $3, and $4 to reference specific
>##           colors from the palette.
>##         - $5 is an optional highlight color (not available in all palettes).
>##
>##    {**<symbol-char> x | y} :
>##         Quick Modifier (cheats).
>##         - If the user's prompt is prefixed with the corresponding
>##           cheat code, the text 'x' is used.
>##         - If no cheat code prefix is detected, the text 'y' is used.
